frontPage.headline: Karnataka Recommends Including SC/ST Reservation Law in Ninth Schedule Following Tamil Nadu Precedent
frontPage.summary: The Karnataka government has requested the Centre to include its enhanced SC/ST reservation law under the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution. Citing Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation framework as a precedent, Karnataka seeks constitutional protection against judicial review for exceeding the 50% ceiling.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Connects directly to GS II Constitutional provisions, Judicial Review, Article 31B, the Ninth Schedule, and the 50% reservation limit established by the Indira Sawhney judgment.

frontPage.headline: India Re-asserts Support for UNGA Resolution on Permanent Sovereignty of Palestinian People
frontPage.summary: India voted in favour of a United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) draft resolution affirming the permanent sovereignty of the Palestinian population in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and the Arab population in the occupied Syrian Golan over their natural resources. The resolution demands an immediate halt to the depletion and endangerment of these resources.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Reflects India's multi-aligned foreign policy and historical stance on the West Asia conflict, highly relevant for GS II International Relations and UN bodies.

frontPage.headline: India's Merchandise Exports Expand 29.9% in October; Trade Deficit Narrows
frontPage.summary: India's merchandise exports recorded a 29.9% year-on-year surge in October 2026, reaching nearly $90 billion total trade value. Strong export volumes outpaced import growth, causing the overall monthly trade deficit to narrow significantly.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Critical data point for GS III Economy covering Foreign Trade Policy, Balance of Payments, trade deficit dynamics, and macro-economic stability.

frontPage.headline: India’s Retail Inflation Breaches RBI's 6% Upper Tolerance Band in October
frontPage.summary: India's retail inflation based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) touched 6.1% in October 2026, crossing the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance threshold of 6% for the first time in two years. Price pressures were seen spreading across multiple broad commodity sectors.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Essential for understanding RBI's Flexible Inflation Targeting framework (4% (+/-2%)), MPC interest rate decisions, and macroeconomic management in GS III.

frontPage.headline: CAG Expands Audit Horizon to Power DISCOM Performance and Consumer Satisfaction
frontPage.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India has broadened its audit scope within the power sector to evaluate State DISCOMs over a five-year period. The expanded audit framework focuses on financial viability, service quality, RDSS scheme execution, and consumer satisfaction.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Combines CAG's constitutional mandate (GS II) with power sector reforms, discom stress, and infrastructure governance (GS III).

frontPage.headline: Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir Dispute Escalates Between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
frontPage.summary: Tensions between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have flared up once again over the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir across the Cauvery River. Karnataka claims the dam will secure drinking water for Bengaluru while ensuring Tamil Nadu's mandated water allocations, whereas Tamil Nadu fears lower riparian rights will be violated.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Key case study for Article 262, Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, and cooperative versus competitive federalism.

gs1.headline: Historical Significance of Hyderabad as Deccan's Central Minting Hub Under the Nizams
gs1.summary: Historians highlighted Hyderabad's central role as the premier minting hub of the Deccan region during the Asaf Jahi (Nizam) dynasty. The region's currency evolution reflects significant economic integration and trade networks across medieval and early modern South India.
gs1.whyItMatters: Useful for GS I Art & Culture / History questions on medieval coinage, regional kingdoms, and economic history.

gs1.headline: Centuries-Old Lavi Fair Highlights Trans-Himalayan Trade and Cultural Exchange in Himachal
gs1.summary: The historic 300-year-old Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, Himachal Pradesh, showcases the historical evolution of Himalayan trade routes between India and Tibet. Traditionally centered on wool, dry fruits, and livestock barter, the fair has transitioned to modern digital trade while maintaining traditional heritage.
gs1.whyItMatters: Frequently asked in Prelims under traditional Indian fairs, trade heritage, and Himalayan tribal economic practices.

gs2.headline: Legal Limits on Serving US Court Summons to Indian National Security Officials Examined
gs2.summary: A U.S. court allowed civil summons to be served via Indian judicial channels on senior Indian security officials. Legal experts point out that under the Hague Service Convention and principles of sovereign immunity, sovereign states retain the right to refuse assistance if service infringes on national sovereignty or security interests.
gs2.whyItMatters: Directly links to international judicial assistance, Hague Service Convention, sovereign immunity, and India-US diplomatic relations.

gs2.headline: Proposed Legislation and State Initiatives for Gig Workers' Social Security
gs2.summary: Policy discussions in Telangana have centered on creating dedicated welfare boards and funding models for platform gig workers. Proposed mechanisms include levying a micro-fee (1%) on transaction values to fund accident cover and healthcare security.
gs2.whyItMatters: Relevant for Code on Social Security 2020 implementation, social safety nets for informal labour, and state welfare policies.

gs3.headline: RBI Proposes Sub-Limit Under Liberalised Remittance Scheme to Protect Domestic Currency
gs3.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has considered a ₹50 lakh sub-cap within the overall $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) ceiling for specific non-essential capital and current transactions. The move seeks to curtail speculative dollar outflows, buffer foreign exchange reserves, and stabilize the domestic rupee.
gs3.whyItMatters: Crucial GS III topic on capital account management, LRS rules, rupee depreciation pressures, and central bank foreign exchange policy.

gs3.headline: National Urgent Need for Formal Lithium-Ion Battery Recycling Ecosystem
gs3.summary: With India's rapid electric vehicle transition, experts urge building a robust domestic closed-loop ecosystem for recycling lithium-ion batteries. Proper recycling ensures recovery of critical minerals like cobalt, lithium, and nickel while preventing severe environmental degradation from unorganized disposal.
gs3.whyItMatters: Spans GS III Environmental Pollution (E-waste rules), Critical Mineral Security, and Sustainable Industrial Policy.

gs3.headline: WHO Global Report Highlights Shift to Domestic Funding for Tuberculosis Management
gs3.summary: According to the latest WHO global findings, domestic allocations now cover 86% of global Tuberculosis funding due to falling international assistance. India accounts for a quarter of the global TB burden, making sustained domestic health infrastructure spending essential for its elimination targets.
gs3.whyItMatters: Directly related to GS III Public Health, National TB Elimination Program targets, and international health finance trends.

gs3.headline: Global One Health Approach Recommended to Counter Rising Antimicrobial Resistance
gs3.summary: Prior to World AMR Awareness Week, global health bodies urged cross-sectoral coordination under the 'One Health' framework linking human, animal, and environmental health. Surveillance and strict regulation of antibiotic misuse in farming and healthcare are highlighted as critical steps.
gs3.whyItMatters: AMR is a frequent subject in UPSC Science & Tech, public health policy, and environmental health challenges.

quiz.question:
Regarding the Ninth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. It was added to the Constitution by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951.
2. Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule are completely immune from judicial review under all circumstances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
quiz.explanation: Statement 1 is correct. The Ninth Schedule was introduced by the 1st Amendment in 1951. Statement 2 is incorrect because in the I.R. Coelho case (2007), the Supreme Court ruled that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973, are open to judicial review if they violate the Basic Structure.

quiz.question: The 'Hera Mission', recently seen in the news, is associated with which of the following?
options: Exploring ice deposits on the lunar south pole
Investigating the asteroid impact site of NASA's DART mission
Studying solar flares from Lagrange Point L1
Monitoring deep ocean currents in the Indian Ocean
quiz.explanation: Hera is the European Space Agency's (ESA) mission designed to perform a detailed post-impact survey of the asteroid Dimorphos, which was struck by NASA's DART spacecraft.

quiz.question:
With reference to the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) of the RBI, consider the following statements:
1. It is available to resident individuals including minors.
2. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can utilize the LRS limit for remitting funds from India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
quiz.explanation: Statement 1 is correct; the LRS facility is available to all resident individuals, including minors. Statement 2 is incorrect because LRS is not available to corporate bodies, partnership firms, or NRIs.

quiz.question: The 'Lavi Fair', famous for its historic trans-Himalayan trade connections, is celebrated in which Indian State/UT?
quiz.explanation: The Lavi Fair is a 300-year-old historic trade fair celebrated in Rampur Bushahr, Himachal Pradesh.

quiz.question: Which institution has proposed setting up India's first dedicated National Poisoning Registry to track clinical poisoning cases?
quiz.explanation: AIIMS New Delhi has initiated plans to launch a National Poisoning Registry to track, monitor, and address poisoning cases across India.

schemes.name: Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS)
schemes.beneficiaries: State Power Distribution Companies (DISCOMs) and electricity consumers
schemes.objective: To improve operational efficiency and financial sustainability of State DISCOMs by providing financial assistance for infrastructure upgradation and smart metering.
keyFeatures: Results-linked financial support to DISCOMs subject to meeting operational targets.
Phased rollout of prepaid smart meters across all consumer categories.
Loss reduction infrastructure including feeder separation and network modernization.
schemes.funding: Centrally Sponsored Scheme with outlay mix of central grants and state/loan funding.
schemes.upscRelevance: High utility for GS III Power & Infrastructure questions and GS II public audit of state utilities.

In I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws included under the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973, are subject to judicial review if they damage the Basic Structure of the Constitution.

Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation protection under the Ninth Schedule via the 76th Constitutional Amendment Act (1994) serves as a precedent currently cited by states like Karnataka to protect enhanced SC/ST quotas.
